notes:
Account background: midsize healthtech vendor supporting hospital charting and billing automation. Exploring moving ML inference from mixed-hosted + self-hosted cluster to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and compliance.

Recent meetings / quotes:
- 2025-01-15 intro call (AE Maya): product overview + ask: ensure 99.95% uptime SLA, cross-region failover, and on-prem fallback for sensitive workloads. Customer: "we cannot have >300ms p95 for clinical assistant queries".
- 2025-01-22 deep-dive with infra & ML (SE Diego): workload profile provided — chat + post-call summarization + embedding syncs. Peak concurrency expected 1500 req/s for embeddings batch windows, average chat QPS 120 with burst to 350.
- 2025-02-01 SLA & cost workshop (procurement + security): procurement pushed back on long termination notice and liability caps; security requested full audit log retention and KMS integration options.

Dedicated evaluation notes (reliability & fallback focus):
- Throughput guarantees: customer expects predictable reserved throughput for nightly batch embeddings and daytime chat. They want a commit that supports sustained 200k tokens/sec across the pool with burst headroom of 2x for 10 minutes.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 < 40ms, p95 < 300ms for single-turn chat (context <= 2k tokens). For longer synth tasks (summarization) acceptable p95 up to 1200ms. Need to confirm model choice and quantization impact with Redwood Optimize.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask is equivalent of 8x A100-class GPUs in primary region + 4x in DR region (warm stand-by). Discussed options: physical reservation vs committed vCPU/GPU hours. Customer preferred hard reserved nodes for consistent latency.
- Cross-region failover: design requirement to fail traffic to EU region when NA primary experiences sustained outage >60s. Must support stateful KV cache sync (or automated cold-start fallback to identical model variant).
- Model variant fallback: plan B is an earlier quantized variant (8-bit) with slightly degraded quality but lower latency/cost. Agree on automated routing policy: prefer high-fidelity model unless CPU/GPU saturation >85%, then route to fallback with real-time metrics and an eval gating signal.
- Observability/traceability: request token-level latency breakdown, per-model tail latencies, and alerts tied to eval sets for quality regressions.

POC scope: 3-week Proof-of-Performance. Deliverables: 1) baseline perf matrix (latency/throughput) for selected model + quantized variant; 2) runbook for manual & automated cross-region failover; 3) SLAs + cost projection for 12-mo reserved capacity; 4) integration doc for on-prem sync and KMS.

Procurement / legal asks still outstanding: uptime SLA thresholds, termination penalties, export controls for EU PHI, and indemnity language. Security to validate KMS + HSM options and retention policy.

Notes from SE (Diego): "We tested a comparable workload ondedicated-like infra: 6 GPU pool hit p95 ~260ms with standard model and ~160ms with quantized variant for short prompts. We need formal runs with customer data and longer context to be confident."
